Why this amount appears in parts
No single amount to compare against

Some part of this period is in a currency with no rate on file, so there is no single amount to compare against — which is why the bar and the proportion are not there. The amounts are still exact, each in its own currency; what is missing is the common measure between them. Add the rate and this works again.
≈ marks an amount that passed through an exchange rate. Where no rate was on file, that currency's share stands on its own, unconverted.

Let an AI agent read and record in the app, on this computer
Did not start — port %1$d in use
While on, the server exists and listens only on 127.0.0.1, on this computer. Turning it on does not decide what an agent can do — that is the permission level.
While off, nothing is listening and no agent reaches your data. While on, an agent on this computer will be able to read your accounts, transactions, invoices and budgets.
The agent reads accounts, transactions, invoices and budgets. The write tools are not announced: as far as it can tell, they do not exist.
Besides reading, the agent creates, changes and deletes transactions on your behalf.
Port %1$d is already in use by %2$s. The server did not start, and no other port is taken in its place: free that port or pick another one.
No agent has written anything yet.
Rotating creates a new token and invalidates the current one. Every client already configured stops connecting until you paste the new configuration into it.
Paste this into your MCP client's configuration file. It already carries the address and the token.
Only an agent running on this computer can reach the server. It will not connect from another device.
The current level is read-only: an agent will connect and see no write operations at all. Change it under Permission, above.
The server speaks revision %1$s of the MCP protocol. A client that speaks another one will not connect.
